title: Attraction from repulsion in an interacting Chern band: chiral superconductivity, generalized Hall crystals, and competing fractional Chern insulators
authors: Fabian Pichler, Clemens Kuhlenkamp, Ashvin Vishwanath, Michael Knap
abstract: Experiments realizing strong interactions in partially filled Chern bands have observed fractional Chern insulators (FCIs), superconductors, and topological crystals in close proximity. Yet the microscopic relation between them remains poorly understood. Here, we use tensor network simulations to study repulsively interacting spinless fermions in a tunable topological band of the checkerboard lattice. We characterize the competing phases and identify key features of the experimental phenomenology. FCIs from the Jain sequence transition into chiral p-wave superconductivity both below and above half filling as the band dispersion is enhanced. By contrast, at half filling, a generalized Hall crystal with quantized Hall conductance and a doubled unit cell forms for sufficiently strong coupling. Surprisingly, a weak-coupling approach starting from a metallic parent state captures the nature of both ordered phases at intermediate coupling. We find that fluctuations in the metal generate longer-range attraction, which we analyze within the random-phase approximation. This approach captures the pairing symmetry as well as the radial form factors of the Cooper pairs, and incorporating this attraction into Hartree-Fock selects the observed Hall crystal. Together, these results identify fluctuation-induced attraction from repulsion as a common microscopic ingredient of ordering, while our tensor network computations establish the direct competition of both phases with FCIs.
summary: This work investigates the complex interplay between competing correlated phases—FCIs, superconductors, and Hall crystals—in interacting Chern bands. Using tensor network simulations and RPA, the authors demonstrate that fluctuation-induced attraction from repulsive interactions serves as the common microscopic mechanism stabilizing these distinct ordered states. The findings provide a unified theoretical picture for understanding correlated topological matter.
main_problem: The paper aims to resolve the poorly understood microscopic relationship between competing correlated phases—Fractional Chern Insulators (FCIs), superconductors, and topological crystals—observed in interacting Chern bands.
main_result: It identifies fluctuation-induced attraction from repulsion as a common microscopic ingredient driving ordering, showing direct competition between FCIs, chiral p-wave superconductivity, and generalized Hall crystals.
method: The study employs a combination of tensor network simulations, Random-Phase Approximation (RPA) for weak coupling, and Hartree-Fock calculations incorporating RPA-derived attraction.
model_or_system: The model consists of spinless fermions with repulsive interactions studied in a tunable topological band on a checkerboard lattice, characterized by a kinetic term, a staggered potential ($\Delta$), and interaction terms.
key_observables: Phase identification (FCI, SC, GHC), charge correlation lengths ($\xi_{2e}/\xi_{1e}$), superconducting gap symmetry, and quantized charge pumping.

main_assumptions: The RPA treatment for effective interactions is perturbative, and the analysis relies on comparing results from different computational techniques (tensor networks vs. weak-coupling approximations).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phase diagram showing transitions between FCI, SC, and GHC as $\Delta$ is tuned, and show evidence of charge pumping confirming FCI states at specific fillings.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical context by reviewing the competing phases. It then uses weak-coupling methods (RPA) to derive an effective attraction, which is shown to stabilize both SC and GHC. Finally, tensor network simulations map the full phase diagram, confirming the competition between these ordered states.
why_interesting: The mechanism of fluctuation-induced attraction from repulsion is a general concept in many-body physics, providing a unified theoretical framework to explain the emergence of superconductivity and charge-density wave order in topological systems.
